systems.title: Ingress
systems.subtitle: Authenticate & normalize
systems.description: Work enters through an authenticated API or a signed provider webhook. Provider-specific requests become an owner-scoped Run request.
facts: API identity determines the owner; a caller cannot supply an arbitrary owner ID.
GitHub, GitLab, Teams and Slack each have their own ingress adapter.

components.title: Control API
components.subtitle: API Gateway · Lambda
components.description: The control API exposes Runs, Things, connections, artifacts and thread continuity to clients and the reference console.
facts: Authenticated requests derive their owner from the principal.
Discovery and schemas describe the installed deployment.

components.title: Signed webhooks
components.subtitle: GitHub · GitLab · Teams · Slack
components.description: Each adapter verifies the provider signature before parsing and normalizing the request.
facts: Invalid signatures are rejected before submission.
The ingress service applies source policy and records trusted provenance.

components.title: Identity context
components.subtitle: Actor ≠ owner ≠ credential subject
components.description: An actor starts work, an owner owns the Run, a source records origin, and a destination determines where the result goes.
facts: Credential subject is distinct from the actor and owner.
Provider payload details stay behind ingress and delivery adapters.

systems.title: Coordination
systems.subtitle: Accept, persist & queue
systems.description: Every accepted execution has one durable Run receipt. The control layer records the request before sending a wake-up to execution.
facts: Things package reusable work as versioned definitions.
Threaded work uses a durable mailbox and a lease to coordinate turns.

components.title: Run service
components.subtitle: One accepted input · one Run
components.description: Submission validates the request, writes its input to S3 and conditionally creates a queued Run before enqueueing it.
facts: An idempotent retry reuses the same request and receipt.
A missed enqueue leaves a durable queued Run that can be recovered.

components.title: Things & schedules
components.subtitle: Reusable, immutable revisions
components.description: Things carry versioned definitions for reusable work. Published revisions can be executed directly or triggered by a schedule.
facts: Draft, test and publish are distinct lifecycle operations.
The scheduler invokes the Thing schedule transport adapter.

components.title: Conversation mailbox
components.subtitle: DynamoDB lease · SQS wake-up
components.description: The coordinator acquires a conversation lease, prepares trusted continuation input and wakes the existing Run for the next turn.
facts: One accepted input remains one public Run, even when it waits for a predecessor.
Checkpoint and turn state let subsequent work continue a conversation.

components.title: Run queue
components.subtitle: Amazon SQS
components.description: The queue carries a Run reference and trace ID to the dispatcher. The request body remains in artifact storage.
facts: Dispatch claims are conditional; duplicate deliveries do not create a second independent Run.
Failed deliveries have a dead-letter queue.

systems.title: Execution
systems.subtitle: An isolated agent runtime
systems.description: The dispatcher launches or resumes a Lambda MicroVM. Trusted orchestration prepares the workspace and runs Codex as a separate non-root process.
facts: The MicroVM is the outer isolation boundary.
The worker has no public user-facing ingress.

components.title: Run dispatcher
components.subtitle: Conditional claim · executor registry
components.description: The dispatcher reads stored input, claims the queued Run and starts its selected executor with a stable execution generation.
facts: A duplicate wake-up is safe after another dispatcher claims the Run.
An execution with the wrong generation is stopped.

components.title: Lambda MicroVM
components.subtitle: ARM64 · launch or resume
components.description: The MicroVM adapter launches an isolated environment, or first tries to resume the preferred conversation MicroVM.
facts: An unavailable prior session can fall back to a new launch.
Conversation continuation goes through the service proxy with an AWS-issued token.

components.title: Codex runner
components.subtitle: Trusted host · non-root agent
components.description: The host prepares workspace files, credentials and allowed tools, starts the agent driver, then records results and artifacts.
facts: Agent processes use argument arrays and a separate UID.
Codex approval requests fail closed; they cannot widen the Run’s authority.

components.title: Browser & tools
components.subtitle: Optional capability
components.description: When enabled for the Run, host-provided browser tools let the agent inspect and interact with a browser in the isolated environment.
facts: Browser actions are routed through the trusted tool handler.
Network and process policy are enforced by the runtime.

components.title: Model access
components.subtitle: ChatGPT / OpenAI · Bedrock
components.description: The runner selects its Codex authentication mode. ChatGPT-backed access and explicit Amazon Bedrock configuration have separate host-side setup.
facts: Model authentication is prepared by trusted runner code.
Provider credentials do not belong in Run requests or repository URLs.

systems.title: Delivery
systems.subtitle: Persist, emit & notify
systems.description: Durable Run state drives completion events. A separate notifier resolves destinations and delivers the result behind a delivery fence.
facts: Completion is emitted from DynamoDB Streams after the state commit.
Terminal events also advance conversation completion.

components.title: State stream & events
components.subtitle: DynamoDB Streams → EventBridge
components.description: Run status changes are published from the table stream, closing the crash window between a state commit and a worker-side event.
facts: The stream handler retries unsuccessful event publishing.
Terminal Run events feed notification and conversation completion.

components.title: Result notifier
components.subtitle: Independent delivery stage
components.description: For a succeeded, failed or cancelled Run, the notifier loads stored input and results, resolves destinations and invokes the provider delivery adapter.
facts: Source-thread replies and configured destinations are resolved separately.
Retries do not require the agent to execute again.

components.title: Delivery fence
components.subtitle: Conditional destination claim
components.description: A DynamoDB fence claims each Run/destination delivery. It records delivered, failed or safely retryable outcomes.
facts: Duplicate terminal events do not blindly send the same result again.
Only known retryable non-delivery releases the claim for retry.

components.title: Artifact publication
components.subtitle: Optional scoped sharing
components.description: Publication services turn selected artifacts into file, video or static-site publications using explicit publication grants.
facts: Publication builders validate and plan output before storage.
Sharing is a separate capability from completing a Run.

systems.title: Durable state
systems.subtitle: Receipts, files & checkpoints
systems.description: State and payloads have different homes: DynamoDB holds records and bounded summaries; encrypted S3 holds prompts, results and artifacts.
facts: Persistent conversations can mount Codex home and workspace through S3 Files.
Storage survives the lifetime of an individual worker.

components.title: DynamoDB records
components.subtitle: Runs · conversations · connections
components.description: DynamoDB stores durable Run state, identities, references and bounded summaries. Conditional writes enforce transitions and leases.
facts: Large prompts and results are stored by reference.
Things, routines and integrations have their own tables.

components.title: Encrypted artifacts
components.subtitle: Amazon S3 · KMS
components.description: Inputs, results and artifact payloads live in S3. Infrastructure configures encryption, public access blocking and retention.
facts: A Run record points to its stored input and output.
Thing definitions use a separate definitions bucket.

components.title: Persistent workspace
components.subtitle: Optional Amazon S3 Files
components.description: When S3 Files is enabled, conversation execution receives a filesystem and access point for durable native state and workspace files.
facts: The adapter includes S3 Files settings only for conversation executions.
A resumed agent can reuse its native thread and workspace.

systems.title: Access boundary
systems.subtitle: Fixed before launch
systems.description: A Run operates inside a fixed capability envelope. Profiles, requested narrowing, IAM, runtime policy and connection grants constrain what it can do.
facts: An operation outside the boundary is unavailable or denied.
There is no mid-Run approval path to expand authority.

components.title: Capability profiles
components.subtitle: Resolve & narrow
components.description: Trusted capability profiles determine the agent configuration. Run and Thing requests can narrow the admitted capabilities.
facts: The runtime resolves an agent profile before running the agent.
Tool availability is constrained by that resolved profile.

components.title: Runtime & IAM policy
components.subtitle: Network · process · resources
components.description: IAM and runtime policies enforce the boundaries around the MicroVM, its network access and its agent process.
facts: The outer environment is the isolation boundary for danger-full-access.
Enforcement denies operations outside the configured envelope.

components.title: Credential broker
components.subtitle: Host-side secret reader
components.description: The host reads and parses secret values through a credential broker. Requests identify allowed resources without carrying provider tokens.
facts: Secrets are held separately from Run metadata and task overrides.
OAuth-backed connections use a host-side vault and refresh broker.

systems.title: Connected services
systems.subtitle: Granted operations & accounts
systems.description: Trusted integration manifests describe operations. The runtime exposes only tools that the selected accounts and their intersected grants allow.
facts: Tool authorization happens before credential access.
Slack, Linear and Stripe integrations are defined in this repository.

components.title: Trusted plugins
components.subtitle: Manifests & adapters
components.description: Provider plugins bind ingress and delivery capabilities. Integration plugins define separate operations for connected services.
facts: The registries validate trusted manifests.
Protocol parsing stays behind provider adapters.

components.title: Connection grants
components.subtitle: Account · operation · resource
components.description: The integration runtime intersects the stored connection grant with requested restrictions and maximum integration access.
facts: Disallowed operations are omitted from the agent’s tools.
Per-call resource checks run before credentials are read.

components.title: Connection lifecycle
components.subtitle: Install · refresh · health
components.description: Connection and OAuth services manage account installation and host-side credentials; a scheduled monitor checks connection health.
facts: Active connections and valid grants are required for tool preparation.
OAuth refresh is separate from guest execution.

systems.title: Recovery
systems.subtitle: Reconcile & retry
systems.description: Recovery is built around durable state. Conditional transitions, execution heartbeats, reconciliation and dead-letter queues handle interruptions.
facts: The domain transition table defines legal Run state changes.
Duplicate deliveries and missing wake-ups are handled explicitly.

components.title: Run state machine
components.subtitle: Conditional transitions
components.description: The Run lifecycle admits only declared transitions. Succeeded, failed and cancelled are terminal states.
facts: A running Run can succeed, fail or enter cancellation.
Terminal states have no outgoing transitions.

components.title: Execution reconciler
components.subtitle: Repair stalled work
components.description: The reconciler inspects active execution and durable Run records to recover work after missed dispatch or worker failure.
facts: Recovery uses the same state and execution ports.
Provisioning tests remain an explicit opt-in operation.

components.title: Heartbeat & dead letters
components.subtitle: Liveness · failed deliveries
components.description: The runner reports execution liveness. Queue and event delivery failures have dedicated dead-letter queues and monitoring.
facts: Heartbeats identify the current execution generation.
Delivery failures remain separate from agent execution failures.

steps.title: Authenticate the request
steps.description: The API derives an owner from the authenticated principal and accepts a Run submission. This example includes a configured result destination.

steps.title: Accept one durable Run
steps.description: Store input in encrypted S3, create a queued receipt and enqueue its reference. An idempotent retry keeps the same receipt.

steps.title: Wake the dispatcher
steps.description: SQS delivers the Run reference and trace ID. The dispatcher reloads the stored request.

steps.title: Claim and launch
steps.description: Conditionally claim the Run and launch or resume its Lambda MicroVM with a stable generation.

steps.title: Run inside the boundary
steps.description: Prepare the workspace and admitted tools, then execute Codex as a separate non-root process.

steps.title: Persist the outcome
steps.description: Write results and artifacts to S3 and commit terminal Run state in DynamoDB.

steps.title: Emit the committed state
steps.description: DynamoDB Streams publishes the state change to EventBridge after the durable commit.

steps.title: Deliver the result
steps.description: The notifier claims a destination fence and delivers the stored result. API clients can retrieve the same Run and artifacts.
